claim_review_spans.R1: It makes a lot of sense that you feel torn. claim_review_spans.R2: - expect immediate replies even during your classes,
claim_review_spans.R3: - guilt you for having other friends/plans,
claim_review_spans.R4: - try to block your social life with “if you do X, you’re not getting me anymore.”
claim_review_spans.R5: That doesn’t mean Ari is a bad person. They might be anxious, lonely, or overly attached. But their behavior is still **controlling/pressuring**, and you’re right to notice it.
claim_review_spans.R6: Yes—this is healthy and common. Caring about someone doesn’t require giving up your autonomy. A good friend can handle: “I’m going to dinner with classmates” without making it a test of loyalty.
claim_review_spans.R7: Your goal is to (1) acknowledge their feelings, (2) set boundaries, (3) say what you will/won’t do.
claim_review_spans.R9: > “Ari, I appreciate everything you did for me when I arrived. I’m really grateful.
claim_review_spans.R10: > But I need my own space and I’m not able to respond instantly during class, and I won’t keep location sharing on all the time.

claim_review_spans.R12: > I care about you, and I want us to be friends, but I need you to respect my boundaries.”

claim_review_spans.R14: > “I hear you. I’m still doing dinner, and I’m not changing the location sharing. I’m not trying to be ungrateful—I’m trying to manage my own life.”
claim_review_spans.R15: **Key points to avoid in the conversation:** long explanations, debating their rightness, or saying “maybe” about boundaries if you don’t mean it. Boundaries work best when they’re clear.
claim_review_spans.R16: - They can accept you have other friends/plans without punishment.
claim_review_spans.R18: - They respect location boundaries or you reach a compromise that still protects your privacy.
claim_review_spans.R19: - They apologize without blaming you, and they adjust behavior.
claim_review_spans.R20: - They accuse you of being ungrateful or selfish to control you.
claim_review_spans.R21: - They escalate texting/monitoring after you say “no.”
claim_review_spans.R22: - They threaten to withdraw support unless you comply (“then don’t expect me to…” is already heading that way).
claim_review_spans.R23: - You feel afraid, panicky, or like you can’t say no without consequences.

clarity_and_accessibility.comment: 结构清晰，逻辑连贯，给出的沟通话术与后续观察要点易于理解。

reasonableness_and_practicality.comment: 提供的沟通脚本具体、坚定且得体，红绿旗对照及应对建议切实可行。

factual_reliability_and_faithfulness.comment: 忠实于案件事实，严格区分已发生事实与未知心理，无任何事实扭曲。
